question: Does a self-check on the measured concentrations make the forecaster uncertainty-aware: narrower calibrated intervals at the same coverage, and better choices of which chemicals receive the full series?

point_model.note: frozen AnchorBoost; point forecasts identical to chip_forecast_result.csv

mechanism.name: self-check
mechanism.definition: A helper AnchorBoost trained on the same training folds with one measured concentration fewer re-predicts each measured concentration from the other measured ones; the self-check score of a design is its mean absolute error over measured concentrations and observed outputs; a chemical score averages its five published designs.

data_and_folds: as chip_forecast_protocol.json: pinned EPA network-formation bundle, five chemical folds, five published context designs, k = 3

intervals.calibration: cross-conformal: for test fold f, per-output quantiles from the held-out well errors of the other four folds, each predicted by its own fold model
intervals.selfcheck: half-width = per-output quantile of |error| / (score + c) times (score + c) of the test design; c = median chemical score of the calibration folds
intervals.primary: width ratio selfcheck/plain (sum of half-widths over wells) with chemical bootstrap 95% interval (4,000, seed 0); pass if self-check coverage lies in [0.88, 0.92] and the ratio interval upper bound is below 1

decisions.rule: chemicals ranked by chemical score; the top share receives the full concentration series, removing its forecast curve error

comparators.random: expected removed share equals the budget

decisions.best_simple: the comparator with the larger removed share at 20% on development fold 0
decisions.primary: removed share self-check minus best simple rule at 20% on folds 1-4, chemical bootstrap 95% interval (4,000, seed 0); pass if the lower bound exceeds 0

development_log.mechanism: analog design replay (residual left by interpolation on the nearest analogs under the same design) as features
self replay errors as point-model features (cross-fitted halves)
cross-size episodes (k-1, k, k+1 designs with size feature)

development_log.conclusion: none of the three moves fold-0 point error beyond 0.003; the point model stays frozen and the self-check score is used for intervals and decisions

compute: free Kaggle CPU, one session per fold; laptop peak memory about 0.5 GB on a subset
